messages:
arjun: quick sync: ran batching + quant sweep for Sparrow-12B on the "GTN-lite" slice. dropping results here for product + ops.
felicia: yay — TL;DR first?
arjun: TL;DR: INT4 gives biggest cost wins but shows measurable regressions on multi-turn instruction and legal/finance slices. INT8 is the pragmatic sweet spot. fp16 retains top fidelity for long docs.
tara: numbers plz.
arjun: unit econ (incl batching & KV effects): fp16 = $1.05 / 1k tokens; INT8 = $0.52 / 1k; INT4 = $0.30 / 1k.
zane: delta quality (macro F1 delta vs fp16 on GTN-lite): INT8 -0.6 pts, INT4 -3.1 pts. hallucination probe (1.5k examples): INT8 +0.5% absolute, INT4 +2.4% absolute.
felicia: latency impact?
arjun: p95 latency (ms): fp16 baseline 210ms, INT8 220ms (+10ms), INT4 260ms (+50ms) — due to slower fallback K/V reconstruction in current INT4 path.
ops-bot: nightly-smoke: pass. build: quant-kernel-regressions: 0. kvcache-hit-delta: INT4 -6.1%, INT8 -1.8%.
tara: ok, we need a single metric for product. I made "Compass" score: Compass = 0.7*QualityNorm + 0.2*CostSavingsNorm + 0.1*LatencyNorm (higher better). cost normalization maps greater savings -> higher.
arjun: pasted normalized snapshot:
```
Variant | QualityNorm | CostSavingsNorm | LatencyNorm | Compass
fp16    | 1.00        | 0.00            | 1.00        | 1.00
INT8    | 0.994       | 0.495           | 0.955       | 0.994*0.7 + 0.495*0.2 + 0.955*0.1 = 0.93
INT4    | 0.969       | 0.809           | 0.806       | = 0.88
```
(note: cost savings normalized to fp16 -> INT4 shows biggest savings but quality drop pulls Compass down)
felicia: Compass prefers INT8 despite INT4 cheaper 9— good. product will want recommended default + routing rules.
arjun: recommendation: default = INT8 for GTN-lite beta. routable exceptions -> fp16 for slices with schema-extraction, contractual/legal, or long-doc (>4k tokens). INT4 = opt-in for high-throughput low-risk pipelines (summaries, simple Q&A) and kept shadowed for 10% traffic to collect failure slices.
tara: routing snippet for engineers?
arjun: use this rule: `route_model = if (metadata.slice in ["legal","finance"] || metadata.context_tokens>4000 || metadata.task=="extraction") then "fp16" elif metadata.traffic_class=="low_risk_high_vol" then "INT4" else "INT8"`
zane: ops/infra: start with 3% canary for INT8 default (because FP16 is prod baseline), shadow INT4 on 10%, and ramp INT8 to 30% after 48h if no regressions.
ops-bot: canary flag created: `feature.gtn.sparrow12b.quant_canary = 0.03`. shadowing config at: infra://configs/gtn/sparrow12b/shadow.json
felicia: product blurb for GTN doc (two lines): "We recommend INT8 for Sparrow-12B as the primary variant for GTN-lite beta — it balances cost and fidelity. Route legal/finance, extraction, and long-doc requests to fp16. INT4 offers deeper cost savings for low-risk high-volume flows but shows notable quality regressions on complex instruction tasks; keep shadowed until kernel fixes.
"
arjun: quick scorecard row for the playbook: [Variant, CostPer1k, DeltaF1, p95_ms] -> INT8, $0.52, -0.6pt, +10ms; INT4, $0.30, -3.1pt, +50ms; fp16, $1.05, 0pt, baseline
tara: follow-ups: 1) PR to gtn/docs with blurb + scorecard (felicia) 2) runtime ticket for INT4 KV-reconstruct perf (assign zane) 3) schedule 48h canary check (ops-bot).
zane: noted, filing runtime ticket now.
felicia: thanks all. will add this to GTN onboarding and ping product for sign-off. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: scheduled re-eval job at 2755630000 to re-run batch after kernel patch attempts.
